content: Hello! how can I help today?
I gave my daughter $40,000 last year. Is that taxable?

Not necessarily. You’ve exceeded the **annual gift exclusion** ($18,000 for 2024), but you can use part of your **lifetime gift exemption**.

Steps:
1. File Form 709.
2. Report the $22,000 excess.
3. Apply it against your lifetime limit (currently $13.61 million).

No tax is due unless you exceed the lifetime cap.
Do I have to pay anything now?
No. The gift just reduces your lifetime exclusion. Gift tax is only due if cumulative gifts exceed that exclusion. Still, **filing Form 709 is mandatory** in your case.
Can my spouse and I both give $18,000?
Yes. You can split the gift and treat $36,000 as excluded—but you must both **sign the Form 709** electing gift-splitting. That reduces or eliminates the excess amount applied to your lifetime limit.
Will this affect estate tax later?
Yes. Every gift above the annual exclusion reduces your available **unified credit**. It lowers the estate exclusion you’ll have at death, so it’s important to track cumulative gifts accurately.
